blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Cybersecurity is how a company protects its information and systems from attacks. Most attacks are not big Hollywood hacks. They are small, everyday tricks: a fake email, a stolen password, a laptop left on a train, or a simple mistake at the wrong moment.

The basics are simple, but they matter a lot. Use strong, unique passwords. Turn on two-factor authentication. Do not click strange links. Lock your screen when you walk away. Report anything that feels wrong, even if you are not sure.

Most companies are hacked because of a small, avoidable habit — not because of a brilliant attacker. Cybersecurity starts with the small things.

items.q: According to the text, what are most attacks like?
items.why: "Most attacks are not big Hollywood hacks. They are small, everyday tricks."

items.q: What should you do when you walk away from your computer?
items.why: "Lock your screen when you walk away."

items.q: The text says you should report something that feels wrong…
options: even if you are not sure
items.why: "Report anything that feels wrong, even if you are not sure."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: Only clever attackers can hack a company.
A fake email can be dangerous.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que empresas são hackeadas por hábitos pequenos e evitáveis, não por atacantes brilhantes.

items.q: "Cybersecurity starts with the small things." This suggests that…
options: only the IT team can help
items.why: Inferência: se começa nas pequenas coisas, os hábitos de cada pessoa fazem diferença.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte no treinamento de novos colaboradores. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team. This is short — just five minutes. I want to give you five simple habits. These five habits stop most of the real problems I have seen in my career.

First, use a strong password. Make it long, and do not use the same one on other websites. Second, turn on two-factor authentication. It sends a code to your phone. It is easy, and it is very strong. Please do it today.

Third, do not click strange links. If an email looks strange, stop and think. Check the name of the sender. When you are not sure, ask me. It is never a silly question, and I am always happy to help.

Fourth, lock your screen. When you leave your desk, lock it. Even for two minutes. It takes one second, and it keeps your work safe.

And fifth, report problems fast. If something feels wrong, tell the IT team. Do not wait, and do not feel bad. A small report today can save the company a big problem tomorrow. That is all. Thank you, and welcome to the team.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How long is Charlotte's talk?
items.why: "This is short — just five minutes."

items.q: What does two-factor authentication do, according to Charlotte?
options: It sends a code to your phone
items.why: "turn on two-factor authentication. It sends a code to your phone."

items.q: What should you do when an email looks strange?
options: Stop, think, and check the sender
items.why: "If an email looks strange, stop and think. Check the sender."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say "It is never a silly question"?
options: She wants new people to feel free to ask
She wants people to work alone
items.why: Inferência: ela incentiva os novatos a perguntar quando têm dúvida, sem medo.

items.q: What is the main message of Charlotte's talk?
options: Security is only the IT team's job
Small daily habits protect the company
New joiners should not use email
items.why: Inferência: ela dá cinco hábitos simples e diz que eles evitam os problemas reais.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our company had a small attack last week." An attack is…
options: an attempt to harm or break in
items.why: Attack = ataque: uma tentativa de causar dano ou invadir.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ your screen before you go to lunch."
items.why: To lock = bloquear a tela quando você sai.

items.q: "I got a fake email from my bank." A fake email is…
options: a real message from a friend
a message that is not true and tries to trick you
an email with a big file
a message from the IT team
items.why: Fake email = e-mail falso, feito para enganar você.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If something feels wrong, ___ it to the IT team."
items.why: To report = relatar, avisar sobre um problema.

items.q: "That mistake was easy to prevent. It was avoidable." Avoidable means…
items.why: Avoidable = evitável: podia ter sido impedido.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre segurança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Please turn on two-factor authentication today." To turn on means to…
items.why: Turn on = ligar, ativar.

items.q: "We will roll out the new password rule next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso para todos, aos poucos.

items.q: "If you get a strange email, please flag it to IT." To flag it means to…
options: point it out as a problem
items.why: Flag it = sinalizar, marcar algo como um problema.

items.q: "Do not log in on public computers." To log in means to…
options: enter your account with your password
items.why: Log in = entrar na conta usando sua senha.

items.q: "Let's follow up on that report tomorrow." To follow up means to…
options: check on it again and take the next step
send it to the wrong team
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, verificar de novo e agir.
